steps.caption: Open Capture.
Speak turns your words into text as you talk, in the browser. You check the text before saving.
Choose the language: English, Hindi / Hinglish or Marathi.
Already have a recording? Use Add files. Open 'Link to a record' to set the language and consent.
Recording language: Hinglish.
Recording consent: who agreed to the recording.
Choose the voice note file.
It is recognised as a Recording. Open it.
In practice mode there is no speech-to-text, so CRE OS asks you to type what was said. The audio is kept.
Type the notes. Here the word Kharadi was heard as 'Karadi'.
Process again.
The transcript is shown. Speakers are not identified, so who said what stays uncertain.
Hinglish was understood: 'bees hazaar sq ft' → 20,000 sq ft, 'March tak' → by March.
'Friday ko options bhejna hai' became a Friday task.
Open the capture review to correct the transcript.
Open 'Correct the note / transcript'.
Fix the misheard word: Karadi → Kharadi.
Save and re-extract. Everything is read again from the corrected text — nothing is duplicated.
Correction history keeps what it was and what you changed it to.
Now a note in Hindi script. Back to Capture.
Type, then write in Hindi (Devanagari).
Save capture.
The note is read in a romanised copy; the receipt shows the same kind of matches.
'Original (Hindi)' keeps the text exactly as you wrote it.
